mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -51.0% to -33.9% over four weeks, signaling sustained recovery momentum. This trend will continue, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks than the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 17.1 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (13.6% above baseline) while RETAIL_REC remains deeply suppressed (-33.9%). This gap signals constrained household mobility. When RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% or RETAIL_REC rises above -25%, pent-up demand will drive retail recovery over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% or RETAIL_REC rises above -25%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise by at least 5 percentage points within two weeks of the trigger condition being met.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -38.6% to -24.9% over four weeks. When WORKPLACES exceeds -20%, commuting routines stabilize and incidental retail visits during work-adjacent hours increase, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 13.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days when WORKPLACES is above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations remain severely suppressed (-37.0%) despite four weeks of recovery. If TRANSIT does not improve by at least 8 percentage points in the next week, public-facing retail will remain constrained because foot traffic from transit-dependent populations cannot recover, keeping RETAIL_REC below -30%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT fails to improve by 8+ percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has improved only 14.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -25% over the next four weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -29%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near baseline (-5.7% at t-0w), indicating essential-trip behavior is normalized. When essential mobility stabilizes, discretionary retail (RETAIL_REC) follows within two weeks as consumer confidence rebuilds and shopping consolidation ends.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±5% of baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -6.0% to -5.7% and stabilized
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve by at least 3 percentage points within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM stabilizing near baseline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated sharply from -6.4% to -24.1% week-on-week, signaling a sudden behavioral shift toward indoor confinement. This reversal indicates a policy tightening or external shock that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, offsetting the prior recovery trend.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 17.7 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite PARKS remaining below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both severely suppressed (-24.9% and -37.0% respectively), indicating coordinated mobility constraints. Only when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve simultaneously by 10+ percentage points will retail foot traffic recover, as this signals coordinated reopening of work and transit infrastructure.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by 10+ percentage points within one week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are the two most suppressed categories
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise by at least 8 percentage points within two weeks of both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improving by 10+ percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation (13.6%) combined with RETAIL_REC suppression (-33.9%) indicates a regime of home-based consumption. If RESIDENTIAL remains above 12% for the next four weeks, outdoor and in-person retail will remain constrained as consumers substitute toward online and home delivery, keeping RETAIL_REC below -30%.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 12% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained stable at 13.6-20.7% across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds -25% while RESIDENTIAL remains above 12% for the entire period.
